key_insight: A large bilingual clinical radiology dataset can train a single vision-language model to answer questions, generate reports, and localize findings spatially without manual annotation.
clinical_relevance: This could help build more scalable radiology AI systems that produce both useful text and spatially grounded outputs for image interpretation workflows.
method: Created RefRad2D, a 1.2M CT/MR image-text dataset from routine clinical practice in German and English.
Automatically built VQA and spatial grounding subsets using LLM-based curation and automated segmentation.
Trained RadGrounder to jointly do report generation, VQA, and grounding via bounding boxes or segmentation.
evidence_signal: On external benchmarks like Slake and VQA-RAD, the model performed competitively, and adding the clinical dataset improved open-ended VQA without reducing language quality.
watch_item: Because the grounding data are automatically generated rather than manually annotated, the quality and reliability of spatial labels may vary and need careful validation.
paper_title: Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision-Language Models for Radiology
